text: Millenarianism Lat. mille , thousand, + annus , year]: Ger. Lehre von dem tausendjährigen Reich ; Fr. doctrine du millénium ; Ital. dottrina dei millenarii . The doctrine of the personal reign of Jesus Christ upon earth, under which the powers of evil are to be restrained and the principles of Christianity to become completely and universally prevalent. The germ of the doctrine is found in the Messianic hope, which prefigured a golden age of temporal as well as spiritual prosperity. The first coming of Christ only partially realized this hope. Hence the expectation, nourished by some of the sayings of Jesus, and especially by the prophecy of John in the Apocalypse, of a second advent at some time in the future, and the re-presentation, under very dramatic circumstances, of a régime under which Christianity should completely triumph. The time of its consummation and the period of its continuance are confessedly indefinite. Literature : A. HARNACK Encyc. Brit., art. Millennium; SCHÜRER, Lehrb. d. neutestamentlichen Zeit-Gesch. (1881), §§ 28, 29; CARRODI, Krit. Gesch. d. Chiliasmus. ( A.T.O. )
